outcomes: A domain authors one strict local manifest for its authority, exports, imports and exact current project bindings
Validation joins producer and consumer declarations, compares them with the resolved Putnami project graph and returns deterministic diagnostics
An adoption baseline can only shrink, while later exceptions remain explicit, temporary and independently reviewable
Humans and automation can inspect the same canonical architecture snapshot without contacting Putnami Cloud
Every snapshot states which dependency classes were actually detected and which were not
nonGoals: Making Putnami Cloud the parser or policy authority
Creating one central hand-maintained matrix of every domain relation
Treating a planned API or event as evidence that the transport exists
Requiring one shared Workspace model or one database per domain
Claiming database, HTTP or event enforcement before those detectors exist
Automatically adding new violations to the frozen adoption baseline

requirements.text: The framework-neutral protocol owns strict parsing, semantic validation, canonicalization, graph comparison, stable finding IDs and ratchet policy; CLI and future agent surfaces reuse it rather than reimplementing its meaning.

Each domain manifest owns its semantic identity and its half of every contract; the generated global graph is a projection and never becomes a second authored authority. A fact on an export whose sole mode is reference may omit data classification metadata; an export that allows any other mode requires both classification and personal-data declarations for every fact.
A planned import cannot carry a current project binding, and a declared transport never creates observed evidence.
The v1 detector compares exact consumer-project to producer-project edges only when both projects map to declared domains; a domain-pair match cannot authorize additional dependencies.
New violations, stale debt entries, expired waivers and additions to a previously committed baseline fail; current baseline debt and live waivers remain visible warnings.
Structured snapshots explicitly report project dependency enforcement for mapped projects and database, HTTP and event observation as not detected in v1.

Framework evidence is compared with the declarations without either becoming the other: an implementation no declaration matches always fails, a declaration is expected to be implemented only inside a domain that already implements something, and the coverage report names the framework-evidence tier rather than claiming runtime observation.

Validation, snapshot and inspection are read-only, discover only exact contained authority filenames outside generated or dependency trees, and read a prior baseline directly from immutable Git objects without checkout.

A darc component takes its declared import as configuration and refuses one the architecture gate would reject. A projection applies the declared freshness bound and missing/stale behavior, orders and de-duplicates updates under the declared late-event rule, gives the write handle only to the writer the local model names, and rebuilds and deletes through the declared strategies. A snapshot version is immutable and addressable. A command refuses an inactive contract and never fails a fire-and-forget caller.
